relations.subject: sdk:field-level-encryption
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - PRIMARY judgment-call relation for this batch. The page explicitly contrasts the two as different tools for different needs, not as the same mechanism under two names: native encryption at rest is comprehensive (whole non-ephemeral buckets, logs, config, audit data) while FLE trades that comprehensiveness for simpler key management on a limited number of fields. This is the strongest available textual evidence in this batch's four pages that the two encryption mechanisms are deliberately distinct, comparably-positioned alternatives - not a naming collision to fold together.
relations.evidence: Server 8.x (and new Capella Operational clusters) offer [encryption at rest](../../../server/current/learn/security/native-encryption-at-rest-overview.md). It's a comprehensive way of encrypting all data in a non-ephemeral bucket, as well as logs, configuration data, and audit data. However, you may prefer the relative simplicity of key management in Field Level Encryption for use cases where there are a limited number of data to be encrypted.

notable_absence.finding: The page states the encryption library 'is subject to the Couchbase License and Enterprise Subscription License agreements' and must be 'explicitly include[d]... as a dependency', which strongly implies Enterprise-only licensing, but it never says the words 'Enterprise Edition' or 'Community Edition' outright the way client-settings.json's TLS relation does ('This feature requires the Enterprise Edition of Couchbase Server'). I declined to assert requiresEdition -> edition:enterprise from this page alone since the evidence gate requires a verbatim statement, and this page's licensing language, while suggestive, does not use that phrase.

cross_component_finding: This page names two disjoint FLE usage modes - annotation-based Jackson data binding (@Encrypted) and manual JsonObjectCrypto field access - that share the same underlying CryptoManager/Keyring/algorithm configuration but are otherwise separate APIs a developer chooses between per use case, matching offersConfigurationChoice's closed-choice shape rather than one being a variant/subtype of the other.
cross_product_finding: PRIMARY FINDING for this batch's central judgment call. This page is the ONE place across all four pages in this batch where Field-Level Encryption (client-side, application-managed keys, field-scoped) and Server's native encryption at rest (server-side, server-managed key hierarchy, whole-bucket-scoped) are named on the same page and explicitly contrasted: 'It's a comprehensive way of encrypting all data in a non-ephemeral bucket, as well as logs, configuration data, and audit data. However, you may prefer the relative simplicity of key management in Field Level Encryption for use cases where there are a limited number of data to be encrypted.' I used tradesOffAgainst rather than hasNoRelationshipTo because the text does not assert the two are simply unrelated - it positions them as comparable alternatives with different strengths (comprehensiveness vs. simplicity), which is a materially different and more informative relationship than the role:* family's collisions, where two things merely share a name with no comparative text at all. This confirms the coordinator's framing was correct to flag this as the batch's central judgment call, and shows the docs themselves already do the disambiguation work explicitly, in one tip box, rather than leaving it for the ontology to infer from a shared word.
